DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City v,mw.dilg.gov.ph DILF OPINION No. 107 s. 2021 Ms. D. CARINA N. JAL-BUENA City Accountant City of Tayabas Province of Quezon Dear Ms. Jalbuena: This refers to your letter dated 23 April 2021 requesting for legal opinion concerning the rightfulness of transaction to be entered into by the Punong Barangay of Angustias Zone 2, Tayabas City, Quezon Province. Per your letter, the Punong Barangay of Barangay Angustias Zone 2 has negotiated for a land located in a different barangay outside its territorial jurisdiction— Brgy. Angustias Zone 3, for the purpose of construction of multi-purpose building— a subsidy from the Tayabas City, Quezon Province. Ostensibly, the Punong Barangay of Angustias Zone 2 has certified that there is no land available in her territorial jurisdiction. Under such premise, arose your query on whether or not the barangay can validly procure a land outside its territorial jurisdiction for the construction of its multi-purpose building At the outset, this Department submits that while local government units (LGUs) are not precluded to procure lands for the purpose of construction of its projects for the benefits of its constituents, the same should be done within its territorial jurisdiction. It is important to note in the herein case that the procurement of land outside the territorial jurisdiction of herein concerned barangay, and subsequently building such multi-purpose hall thereat would ipso facto alter the territorial boundaries of the barangays concerned. Such case finds no basis in law. It is equally important to note that although territorial boundaries of LGUs may be altered pursuant to the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160), the same should be done thru an ordinance duly enacted by the sanggunian concerned, and not just by a mere negotiations entered into by the local chief executive, such as the case at bar. Section 6 of the Local Government Code provides, thus: "Section 6. Authority to Create Local Government Units. — A local government unit may be created, divided, merged, abolished, or its boundaries substantially altered either by law enacted by Congress in the case of province, city, municipality, or any other Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

political subdivision, or by ordinance passed by the sangguniang panlalawigan or sangguniang panlungsod concerned in the case of a barangay located within its territorial jurisdiction, subject to such limitations and requirements prescribed in this Code." As could be gleaned from the aforequoted provision, boundaries of LGUs, specifically barangays, may be altered thru the passage of an ordinance by the concerned sangguniang panlalawigan or sangguniang panlungsod, as the case may be. Absence of such ordinance would render any alterations to the territorial boundaries of LGU legally infirm. Further, Section 11 of the Local Government Code states, thus: "Section II. Selection and Transfer of Local Government Site, Offices and Facilities. - (b) When conditions and developments in the local government unit concerned have significantly changed subsequent to the establishment of the seat of government, its sanggunian may, after public hearing and by a vote of two-thirds (2/3) of all its members, transfer the same to a site better suited to its needs. Provided, however, That no such transfer shall be made outside the territorial boundaries of the local government unit concerned. The old site, together with the improvements thereon, may be disposed of by the sale or lease or converted to such other use as the sangguniang concerned may deem beneficial to the local government unit concerned and its inhabitants. (c) Local government offices and facilities shall not be transferred, relocated, or converted to other uses unless public hearings are first conducted for the purpose and the concurrence of the majority of all the members of the sanggunian concerned is obtained." It could be deduced from the foregoing provisions how the law has put emphasis on the sanctity of the territorial boundaries of a local government unit. Beyond its boundaries, acts of local government unit are deemed ultra vires. In view of the foregoing, herein subject query should be answered in the negative. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. Very truly yours, By the Authority of the Secretary: Page 2 of 3

B. DINO MA ndersecretary for Barangay Affairs OUSBNMBD/LLLS-LRALLD/jam DIR. ARIEL IGLESIA Regional Director, DILG-Region IV-A 3/F Andenson Bldg. 1 , National Highway Barangay Parian. City of Calamba, Laguna Page 3 of 3
